description: Moves a webinar to another date, clock time, timezone or length, on an existing webinar and without rebuilding anything; for an evergreen webinar it changes the recurring air-times. Side effect: it writes on the connected WordPress site, the participant pages show the new date at once and the reminders that belong to the time move with it; the texts are not rewritten. Needs `session_id` and `webinar_id` from wi_list_webinars. `start_date` is YYYY-MM-DD and only for a live webinar, `start_time` a clock time such as 15:30, `start_timezone` an IANA id such as Europe/Berlin, `duration_minutes` how long the webinar runs. For an evergreen webinar pass `schedule` instead of a date: {timezone, instant_access, blocks:[{time:"HH:MM", weekdays:["mon","wed","fri"]}]}. A bare hour with no am/pm is refused as ambiguous, never guessed. Name the stored start the answer reads back and quote its affected_places_line, so the host sees every place the new date shows.

duration_minutes.description: How long the webinar runs, in minutes (1-1440).

schedule.description: Evergreen only: {timezone, instant_access, blocks:[{time, weekdays}]} with up to three air-times.

session_id.description: From an earlier turn (weiter · texte · stand).

site.description: Which connected site is meant when this chat has more than one: the address exactly as wi_get_connector_status lists it under sites. Leave it out while only one site is connected.

start_date.description: The new live start date as YYYY-MM-DD. Leave it out for an evergreen webinar.

start_time.description: The new clock time, e.g. 15:30. A bare hour with no am/pm is refused as ambiguous.

start_timezone.description: The IANA timezone of that time, e.g. Europe/Berlin.

webinar_id.description: The webinar (campaign) id, as wi_list_webinars returned it. Never invent an id.

name: wi_change_webinar_schedule
title: Change when a webinar runs
